title: Delhi Lakshmi Yojana: Over 1.45 lakh women register for the cash transfer scheme, says Govt
content:
• The 'Delhi Lakshmi Yojana' online portal was launched by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on 1 August, with the BJP government allocating ₹5,100 crore for the scheme.
• Eligible women under the scheme will receive financial assistance of ₹2,500 per month, with ₹1,500 of this amount kept in a fixed deposit with a three-year lock-in period and ₹1,000 provided directly every month.
• A mandatory requirement for applying to the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana is the submission of a letter of recommendation signed by the applicant's local MLA or MP.

title: Petrol, diesel prices today — 3 Aug: Fuel rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru as Brent falls on US-Iran deal optimism
content:
• Domestic retail fuel rates have remained steady for over two months, with the last major price adjustment occurring on May 25.
• On August 3, Brent crude oil prices declined by 7.3% to $81.55 a barrel, after having climbed $32 last month following a June truce collapse.
• In July, major Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) including Indian Oil Corp (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd (HPCL) recorded a 9.7% year-on-year increase in petrol sales to 3.45 million tonnes, and a 10.7% rise in diesel sales to 7.12 million tonnes.

title: US-Iran war news LIVE: Trump says Iran talks to take place on Monday, refuses to set a deadline for a peace deal
content:
• US President Donald Trump announced on August 2 that talks with Iran would take place on Monday (local time).
• Oil prices tumbled on Monday, with Brent North Sea crude down 4.69 percent at $83.81 per barrel for September delivery.
• Indian equity markets opened sharply higher on Monday, with Sensex soaring over 700 points and Nifty crossing the 24,500 level.

title: Iran says no deal to reopen Hormuz, denies asking Trump to pause strikes: What we know so far
content:
• On Sunday, August 2, Iran rejected US President Donald Trump's claims of an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and of Iran requesting a pause in military strikes.
• Iran asserted that the strategic Strait of Hormuz would remain closed as long as the United States continued 'hostile actions,' requiring vessels to obtain authorization and pay transit fees for passage.
• The US State Department issued security alerts across the Middle East, advising American citizens in Bahrain, Israel, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates to prepare for travel disruptions.

title: RBI MPC begins today as policymakers weigh inflation, crude risks
content:
• The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) began its three-day meeting on Monday, with expectations for the benchmark repo rate to remain unchanged in the August policy review.
• CPI for the full year is estimated at 4.9 per cent by Maulik Patel, Head of Research at Equirus Securities, driven by petrol/diesel price increases and weather disturbances.
• Equirus Securities anticipates a 25-basis-point rate hike in the December policy review, with warnings that prolonged crude oil prices in the USD 90-100 per barrel range could strengthen the case for rate hikes in the second half of the fiscal year.

title: RBI special windows seen big enough to bring in $100B
content:
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that its special programmes mobilized $40.81 billion in foreign exchange inflows up to July 31.
• Of the total inflows, FCNR(B) deposits accounted for $36.72 billion, with the current FCNR(B) programme operational since June 8.
• The FCNR(B) window, announced by RBI on June 5, remains open until September 30, while the ECB and OFCB windows will be available until December 31.

title: India, Canada aim to conclude CEPA trade pact by end-2026: MEA
content:
• India and Canada aim to conclude the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) trade pact by late 2026.
• Bilateral trade between India and Canada stood at $8.66 billion in 2024-25, comprising exports worth $4.22 billion from India and imports of $4.44 billion.
• Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh announced that the third round of CEPA negotiations was held in Ottawa from July 6-10.

title: Indian companies build inventories amid rising commodity prices, supply chain risks: Report
content:
• According to Bajaj Broking's August Monthly Outlook report, banks and financial institutions maintained stable asset quality and recorded healthy loan and credit growth during the April-June quarter (Q1FY27).
• India's economy showed resilience in Q1FY27 with average industrial production growth of 5.7 per cent and average services production growth of 15.3 per cent during the first two months of the quarter.
• The Ministry of Finance, in its July Monthly Economic Review, projected domestic demand to remain resilient despite commodity price volatility.

title: RBI likely to hold rates in August, maintain hawkish tone as inflation risks loom: Economists
content:
• The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is set to meet from August 3 to August 5, with economists expecting the benchmark repo rate to remain unchanged.
• As per the news, Governor Sanjay Malhotra has reiterated inflation as the central bank's foremost priority, with the RBI expected to maintain a 'Neutral' policy stance but adopt a 'hawkish tone' in August.
• The RBI has reduced the repo rate by 1.25 per cent since last year, and some economists, like Balasubramanian R of Dhanlaxmi Bank, anticipate the FY27 retail inflation projection to be raised to 5.1 per cent.

title: RBI MPC likely to stay on hold amid inflation risks, global uncertainty
content:
• The Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is expected to keep the benchmark repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent at its August 3-5 meeting.
• Headline retail inflation accelerated to 4.4 per cent in June from 3.9 per cent in May, breaching the RBI’s 4 per cent target for the first time since January 2025 and touching an 18-month high.
• In June, the RBI raised its FY27 inflation forecast to 5.1 per cent from 4.6 per cent and lowered its GDP growth projection to 6.6 per cent from 6.9 per cent.
